candidate.answerReason: Emily gains 1 mile on Emerson during the visibility interval at a relative speed of 4 miles per hour. This takes one-quarter hour, or 15 minutes.

methods.label: Track the distance Emily gains
methods.explanation:
Emily first sees Emerson \(\frac12\) mile ahead and last sees him \(\frac12\) mile behind. During that interval, she gains a total of
\[
\frac12+\frac12=1\text{ mile}
\]
on him.

Because they travel in the same direction, Emily gains distance at \(12-8=4\) miles per hour. The time needed to gain \(1\) mile is therefore
\[
1\div4=\frac14\text{ hour}.
\]
Since an hour contains \(60\) minutes, she can see Emerson for \(\frac14\cdot60=\boxed{15}\) minutes, choice D.
methods.levelReason: Uses subtraction of same-direction speeds, distance divided by speed, and elementary time conversion.

candidate.annotationRationale: The target is interpreting a same-direction travel interval through the distance gained. The distance-speed-time relationship and hour-to-minute conversion support that reasoning; linear-equation modeling is unnecessary.

review.mathematicalCheck: Emily gains 1/2+1/2=1 mile during visibility. Her speed relative to Emerson is 12-8=4 miles per hour, so the interval is 1/4 hour, or 15 minutes.
review.levelCheck: The explanation connects the visibility endpoints to distance gained and uses only elementary travel arithmetic and time conversion.
